MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA Automation Engineer | CI/CD & Platform Infrastructure
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including recent work on CI/CD pipelines, test infrastructure and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines and Helm-based ephemeral test environments for three product teams. Personal infrastructure projects include a k3s cluster with GitOps and Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS infrastructure. Currently preparing for the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam; not yet certified.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Terraform (personal project), Ansible (basic)
Containers & GitOps: Kubernetes (namespace-level access; test environments), k3s, Argo CD
Monitoring & observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki
Programming & scripting: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Systems & data: Linux, Git, PostgreSQL
Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (free-tier learning); Hetzner VPS

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering builds, unit/integration/e2e tests and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating e2e testing into its own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%.
- Built short-lived, merge-request test environments for applications, PostgreSQL and seeded data, deployed through GitLab CI using Docker Compose and later Helm on the shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright e2e suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Developed Bash and Python tools for PostgreSQL test-data seeding.
- Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and created Grafana dashboards to help teams identify flaky tests.
- Wrote an internal guide to the CI system used in onboarding.
- Mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Performed manual and automated testing of web and mobile applications across client projects.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs for nightly regression runs.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT

Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal project | 2024–2025
- Set up a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Configured Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATION & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam preparation; exam booked for January 2027 (not yet certified)

LANGUAGES
Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, professional, and substantially stronger than the original source CV. It uses clear section headings, quantified achievements, relevant technologies, and honest qualification wording such as “namespace-level access” and “not yet certified.” The strongest evidence includes reducing pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes, reducing CI runner costs by approximately 30%, managing approximately 900 tests, and reducing flaky tests below 1%. The infrastructure project section adds useful evidence of self-directed learning. The main content limitation is that the CV presents strong QA/test-infrastructure experience but only limited direct cloud infrastructure experience, so its positioning for a Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role remains transitional rather than fully matched.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly: standard headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, text-based content, clear job titles, and relevant keywords including GitLab CI, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, AWS, Linux, PostgreSQL, Prometheus, Grafana, TLS, and CI/CD. It should parse reliably and has a good AI-screening probability for junior-to-mid DevOps, platform engineering, CI/CD, and test-infrastructure roles. Screening probability for this specific contractor role is moderate because the CV does not contain the required Terragrunt, mTLS, system design, networking, or cloud-production terminology, and it does not show direct AWS operating experience. This is primarily a genuine experience-alignment limitation rather than an ATS formatting defect. The explicit labels “personal project,” “basic,” “learning,” and “not yet certified” are appropriate and protect credibility.
critique.job_alignment_feedback:
The CV aligns well with hands-on CI/CD infrastructure, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes-adjacent work, Linux, monitoring, Terraform experimentation, technical documentation, analytical problem-solving, and some technical leadership. It also provides credible evidence relevant to the company’s ownership-oriented and collaborative culture: the candidate owns pipelines for three teams, wrote onboarding documentation, mentored interns, and created environments that allow QA and product teams to review changes.

The candidate's material shows genuine gaps against the role's cloud-platform expectations: no Terragrunt, no demonstrated strong Terraform use, no mTLS experience, no explicit production AWS operation, no IoT/automotive or remote-device integration, and no backend/full-stack experience beyond Java test code. The candidate also has not operated the Kubernetes cluster itself or performed production on-call, although those are not explicitly listed as requirements. The CV should therefore emphasize truthful adjacent experience rather than imply full ownership of cloud architecture or cluster operations.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES:
None. No unsupported skills, certifications, tools, or experiences were detected when compared with the Original Candidate Information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Experience section under “QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software,” revise the ephemeral-environment bullet to make the design contribution and operational boundary clearer: “Designed and maintained short-lived merge-request test environments for applications, PostgreSQL, and seeded data; deployed through GitLab CI using Docker Compose and later Helm on the shared Kubernetes cluster, with namespace-level access. Environments were automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.” This better supports the ad’s infrastructure-engineering and system-design language without implying ownership of the Kubernetes cluster.

2. In the same Odrava experience section, add the supported stakeholder outcome to the ephemeral-environment bullet or as a second sentence: “The environments enabled QA and product teams to review features before merge and run end-to-end tests against isolated deployments.” This makes the candidate’s collaboration and stakeholder-enablement experience more visible for the requirement about bringing stakeholders along.

3. In the Professional Summary, replace “Personal infrastructure projects include a k3s cluster with GitOps and Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS infrastructure” with “Alongside production CI/test-infrastructure work, built a personal three-node k3s cluster with GitOps, observability, TLS ingress, and Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS infrastructure.” This gives the project stronger architecture and operations context while preserving the personal-project distinction.

4. In the Technical Skills section, change “Terraform (personal project)” to “Terraform (personal Hetzner infrastructure project)” and retain “AWS EC2 and S3 basics (free-tier learning).” This makes the scope of the cloud experience immediately clear to both recruiters and ATS/AI screening systems and avoids any impression of professional AWS or Terraform ownership.

5. In the Selected Infrastructure Project section, expand the “Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps” bullets to include the candidate’s supported Ansible experience: “Provisioned supporting infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and basic Ansible.” Do not describe Terraform or Ansible as production experience or add Terragrunt.

6. In the Professional Summary or the first Odrava bullet, use the exact supported phrase “technical infrastructure topics” without overstating formal leadership: for example, “Owns CI/CD and test-infrastructure topics for three product teams serving approximately 25 developers.” This improves alignment with the requirement to lead technical topics while remaining consistent with the source material.

7. Keep the CKA wording exactly qualified as “exam preparation; exam booked for January 2027 (not yet certified).” Do not shorten it to “CKA” in the headline, summary, or skills section, because that could be misread as a completed certification.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, professional, and supported by strong quantified achievements. The infrastructure project adds useful evidence of self-directed learning. The main content concern is that the current employment title may overstate the candidate’s official position relative to the original information, even though the responsibilities are accurately described. The document also presents a strong DevOps trajectory but does not establish the deeper cloud architecture, networking, security, or Terraform/Terragrunt experience expected for this contractor role.

The explicit qualification note—“not yet certified”—is appropriately transparent. AI screening probability is moderate to good for junior or mid-level DevOps/platform roles, but weaker for this specific contractor role because Terragrunt, mTLS, networking, security, system design, and production cloud operations are not supported. The skills section is generally parsing-friendly and responsibly labels Terraform as a personal project and AWS as basic learning.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV shows credible hands-on infrastructure-adjacent engineering: CI/CD ownership for three teams, ephemeral Kubernetes test environments, Helm, Docker Compose, observability dashboards, Linux, and personal Terraform/k3s work. It also shows analytical thinking and communication through measurable pipeline optimization, flaky-test analysis, an onboarding guide, and mentoring. AWS exposure is present but only at basic free-tier learning level, which is weaker than the ad’s preferred cloud-environment experience. The candidate’s material does not support strong Terraform or Terragrunt, mTLS, broader network design, practical production security ownership, IoT/automotive integration, or backend/full-stack engineering. The documented Kubernetes access is namespace-level and the shared cluster is operated by another platform team, so the CV should not imply full cluster ownership or production platform operations. The role is therefore a partial match, strongest for CI/CD and test-platform infrastructure, but not yet a strong match for the advertised cloud infrastructure contractor scope.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Professional Experience section, change the current title “DevOps Engineer | Odrava Health Software” to the candidate’s supported title, such as “QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software.” Keep the DevOps/platform scope visible in the bullets and headline rather than presenting an unsupported official job title. This avoids a potential title misrepresentation while preserving the truthful relevance of the work.

MINOR — In the Odrava Health entry, make the scope limitation explicit in the Kubernetes bullet by changing “deployed through GitLab CI using Docker Compose and later Helm on the shared Kubernetes cluster” to wording such as “deployed through GitLab CI using Docker Compose and later Helm to namespace-level environments on the shared Kubernetes cluster.” This more precisely reflects the candidate’s documented access and avoids implying cluster administration.
critique.critical_issues: Potential title misrepresentation: the CV lists the current role as “DevOps Engineer,” while the original candidate information identifies the role as “QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure).” The responsibilities support a DevOps/platform transition, but the official title is not supported as written. Fix by using the supported title and describing the DevOps scope in the headline and achievement bullets.
